subject: Generate samples from log-volatility of SV models

messages.author: 6ef9ff9f8ade4a18
messages.subject: Generate samples from log-volatility of SV models
parts:
Hi everyone!

I've been using INLA to fit a simple stochastic volatility model, with Student-t distribution. However, I was trying to generate samples from the log-volatility with the inla.rmarginal method, using the marginal from the log-volatility, which I suppose is the inla.hyperpar$marginals.random. I can also see that the method marginals.random contains several indexes, for example inla.hyperpar$marginals.random[[1]]$index.1 up to 1400 (which is my series length). Unlike the other hyperparameters, I'm not being able to get those samples. 

So my question is, am I going to the right direction or should I try something different?

Thanks in advance,
Marcos

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Generate samples from log-volatility of SV models
parts:
Hi

the inla.rmarginal will generate samples for on marginal. if you want
samples from the joint fitted model, you have to use
inla.posterior.sample() or inla.hyperpar.sample(). see their help
pages. you may want to compute also the marginals for the linear
predictor, by setting the option control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE)

H

Thanks a lot for the quick reply! That was exactly what I was looking for.

However, when I use the inla.posterior.sample(1, result) method I'm getting this results:

List of 1
 $ :List of 3
  ..$ hyperpar: Named num [1:3] 46.5 1.753 0.993
  .. ..- attr(*, "names")= chr [1:3] "degrees of freedom for stochvol student-t" "Precision for time" "Rho for time"
  ..$ latent  : num [1:2821, 1] 0.356 0.304 0.315 0.422 0.588 ...
  .. ..- attr(*, "dimnames")=List of 2
  .. .. ..$ : chr [1:2821] "Predictor:0001" "Predictor:0002" "Predictor:0003" "Predictor:0004" ...
  .. .. ..$ : chr "sample1"
  ..$ logdens :List of 3
  .. ..$ hyperpar: num -4.02
  .. ..$ latent  : num 7923
  .. ..$ joint   : num 7919

The doubt that I have now is related to the sample size of the latent variable. Since the series size is n=1410, shouldn't the sample of the latent variable be also a size 1410?

Once again, thanks a lot for the help.

Bests,
Marcos

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Generate samples from log-volatility of SV models
parts:
if n is the data length, then you'll will, with the model

y ~ 1 + f(time, model="ar1")

have the latent vector = (linear.predictor, ar1, intercept)

which is n + n + 1 = 2*n + 1.
